questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Amsterdam seemed like a great university offering a range of interesting subjects at the faculty of political science, which I found super interesting and relevant. The city of Amsterdam seemed like a super chill and nice city to be studying in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Amsterdam was really good at providing the relevant information on their websides and the exchange office as well as study advisors were always helpful and available.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance from study advisors to choose the right subjects.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult. The housing market in Amsterdam is quite crazy so you should be prepared to start your house search early on. I travelled to Amsterdam a couple of months before my exchange semester began in order to meet up with rental firms. Many housing companies did not want to rent out to students or had a minimum rent period of a year.. So start your house search early!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Many lovely parts of the city to live in. Expensive to live in the areas of De Pijp and Jordaan, but super cool and nice neighborhoods. Cheaper to live in West or South which are also nice areas.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All information was easily made available. But a little bit confusing with several platform for registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistance and guidance from exchange office where the study advisors were super helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The classes that I wanted at the Social and Behavioural Sciences faculty in the Poltiical Science programme filled up really quickly and because it was first come, first service principle, I was quite dissatisfied with the courses which I eventually got registrered in. Yet, by reaching out to the international office I was able to register for some of the courses that I initially wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fortunately I think the plan was that the registration system would be changed making it easier to choose courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Quite heavy study load. The semester is divided into 3 blocks, with the 3rd block in January. I chose to only take courses in the first two blocks which made the study load quite heavy - but it was manageable and really interesting courses. Be aware that their grading system is quite different with scores from 5,5 to 10, and it is almost impossible to get a grade above 8. So do not expect to receive top grades.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar. Yet, my courses

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Political Economy, Introduction to Conflict Studies and Conflict, Security and Developmemtn

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above. Super interesting political science courses.

questions.answer: Everything you can think of.. Very good social environment, lots of social clubs and activities to attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed USC sports for yoga, pilates and fitness. Cheap membership.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Areas: De Pijp, Jordaan. Parks, take the ferry to Noord, go on weekend trips to Utrecht, Rotterdam or Harleem. Go to Stedelijk Museum. Visit Cafe Chris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - the Dutch are quite similar to Danish people :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Quite similar culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Directness, everyone biking, beer lovers :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for quite heavy study load, get a bike from Swapfiets, and visit the areas of Jordaan and De Pijp! + the beers are super cheap :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam is a really great city and the University is truly recommendable!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Studying in an international environment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing.
